leading_projects.name: TileLang-TPU
leading_projects.summary: A TileLang backend for SOPHGO TPUs, from compile-time memory planning to executable kernels.
leading_projects.overview: TileLang-TPU brings tile-level programming to commercial SOPHGO accelerators. It preserves the TileLang programming model and turns on-chip memory placement, data movement, and transfer–compute overlap into compiler decisions. The compiler and JIT runtime provide an end-to-end path from a Python kernel definition to execution on BM1690.

highlights.title: Static memory allocation
highlights.description: Assign concrete local-memory offsets at compile time, accounting for alignment, capacity, and memory-bank placement.

highlights.title: Structured pipeline lowering
highlights.description: Turn tiled loops into explicit execution stages so that data transfers can overlap with computation while preserving dependencies.

highlights.title: Backend mapping and runtime
highlights.description: Generate TPU kernel API calls and connect the output to host/device compilation, linking, loading, and launch.

evaluation.hardware: SOPHGO BM1690, single card, PCIe mode
evaluation.metric: PPL kernel latency / TileLang-TPU kernel latency
evaluation.scope: Five kernels × five input shapes × three data types on one SOPHGO BM1690 card. Average speedup over PPL uses TPU kernel execution latency; compilation and host execution are outside this timing.
evaluation.methods: Both implementations use the same operator semantics, shapes, data types, and vendor compilation toolchain. Each case uses five warm-up runs and ten timed repetitions. The reported set includes 71 faster cases, one tie, and three slower cases.

leading_projects.name: TileLang-RISC-V
leading_projects.summary: Bringing TileLang to RISC-V CPUs with AME matrix acceleration. An ongoing effort with open-source hardware and systems researchers.
leading_projects.overview: This project is developing a TileLang backend for RISC-V AME AI CPUs, in collaboration with the Beijing Institute of Open Source Chip and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Current work focuses on connecting the programming model to target instructions and establishing a usable compilation and execution path.

highlights.title: Programming model
highlights.description: Express common AI operators with tile-level programs and identify the information the backend needs.

highlights.title: Target integration
highlights.description: Connect compiler lowering, AME instruction mapping, and the execution environment.

highlights.title: Evaluation
highlights.description: Test operator correctness and performance across target configurations, and use the results to guide backend optimization.
